transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Ruiz (CTO - PocketFrame), Samir Khan (ML Eng - PocketFrame), Toby Lee (Infra Lead - PocketFrame)

Summary:
Brief discovery for PocketFrame planning an exit from current hosted vendor (OpenAI/Azure OpenAI) toward a mix of Redwood Hosted -> Dedicated or Private. Main concerns: latency P95, cost per token, private VPC/KMS requirements, and eval parity for current prompts running on vLLM/TGI. Customer wants clear path and minimal regressions plus auditability.

Topics covered:
- Current stack and pain (OpenAI costs, flaky rate limits, VPC needs)
- Performance parity (vLLM/TGI equivalence) and benchmarking approach
- Hosting options: Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (on-prem/VPC)
- Security/compliance: SOC 2, KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs
- Next steps and initial POC scope

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Ravi, our SE who'll be doing the deeper perf and private deploy work.
[00:12] Elena: Hi Maya, hi Ravi. I'm Elena, CTO at PocketFrame. We have Samir and Toby with me. Quick context — we've been on a hosted provider for two years and costs have spiked, rate limits bite during big ingests, and we need better control for data residency.
[00:25] Samir: Yeah, cost per token is up, and our inference stack is vLLM on a couple of TGI forks — it's a little home-grown. So parity concerns first, also how much work to move the prompt set.
[00:40] Ravi: Got it. Quick question on the vLLM/TGI mention — are you running vanilla vLLM or a fork with custom kernels?
[00:47] Samir: Mostly vanilla vLLM but we have a patched attention kernel, and some batching logic in the serving layer. We also use striping across three nodes.
[00:58] Toby: From infra side, we need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS; some of our customers demand HSM-backed key storage. SOC 2 is table stakes.
[01:10] Maya: Totally reasonable. For that profile we normally discuss Dedicated pools or a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem). Redwood supports KMS integrations and HSM options via our private offering, and audit logs + RBAC are available.
[01:22] Elena: How close will outputs be to our current host? We can't afford drift on production prompts — even small shift in tokenization behavior or sampling could change downstream metrics.
[01:35] Ravi: Parity is the big one. We typically run an eval parity suite: your canonical prompt set, sampling seeds, and a small holdout dataset to compare generation quality and safety filters. For vLLM/TGI parity we benchmark both latency and output diffs. We also look at deterministic sampling if you need exact match.
[01:51] Samir: Sounds good. Do you run the same tokenizer? We had issues once when switching runtimes and token counts changed by a few percent.
[01:58] Ravi: We preserve tokenizer binaries and support the same tokenizers — but note sometimes tokenization differences show up when a different tokenizer version or BPE merges are used. We recommend shipping your tokenizer artifacts with the eval suite.
[02:10] [small crosstalk] Elena: Also can Redwood handle our mixed workload? We do short chat interactions and long doc summarization — very different sequence lengths.
[02:20] Maya: Yes, our runtime has sequence-aware kernel selection and autoscaling policies tuned per model and route. For long sequences we can recommend quantized variants or split-route designs to control cost.
[02:34] Toby: On dedicated: what's the minimal commitment? We prefer predictable throughput but don't want to overcommit.
[02:41] Maya: Typical reserved capacity starts at the 8xA100 pool for mid-sized teams. We can do monthly or annual. For initial POC, we can provision smaller burstable capacity and emulate production load for benchmarks.
[02:55] Samir: Any hard numbers on P95 we should expect moving off our vendor? Right now our P95 on short-chat is ~120ms at peak — that's measured on vLLM with some tuned kernels.
[03:07] Ravi: On Redwood Hosted with similar model variants, 100-160ms P95 for short-chat is common depending on model size and batching. For Dedicated with custom kernel tuning you can push lower — sometimes hitting 80–100ms P95. But that depends on batch strategy and KV cache hit rate.
[03:24] Elena: KV cache — how is that persisted across instances? We worry about cold-starts on the first request.
[03:31] Ravi: We use a distributed KV cache for prefixes; warm caches are sticky per pool. For cold starts we recommend a prewarm policy on Dedicated or run a warm-up traffic replay during boot. That reduces cold tail dramatically.
[03:44] [pause] Samir: Let's talk about cost. Right now token cost with our vendor is high; what levers do you give us?
[03:51] Maya: Redwood Optimize provides batching suggestions, model quantization profiles, and route-level caching. Combined, customers typically see 20–60% unit cost reduction when they adopt quantized models and prefix caching.
[04:05] Toby: And network egress for Private deploys? Some of our customers are EU-only and have strict residency.
[04:12] Ravi: With Private you control the VPC — egress is your environment's cost. We support regional deployments to satisfy residency and a private control plane option to minimize data leaving your network.
[04:25] Elena: Ok. Security specifics — SSO, SAML, audit logs, data retention, are those ready off the shelf?
[04:33] Maya: Yes: SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC, long-term audit logs (configurable retention) and integration with customer KMS. We'll send the security pack with SOC2 and HIPAA addenda.
[04:44] Samir: For the POC technical scope, can we get a short SE-led test where you run our prompt set against your Hosted and Dedicated variants to see latency and output deltas?
[04:56] Ravi: Absolutely. Typical approach: 1) you share prompt set + tokenizer + 1000 sample messages, 2) we run generation on Redwood Hosted and a Dedicated node (or private if needed), 3) we produce perf and diff reports. We'll also capture token counts and sampling parameters for reproducibility.
[05:14] [interruption/noise] Speaker 1: Sorry, noise — continue.
[05:20] Toby: We have one more constraint — some of our higher-tier customers demand HSM-backed KMS and signed audit trails for key rotations. Is that supported?
[05:29] Maya: Yes, for Private deployments we can integrate with HSM-backed KMS and provide signed logs and key rotation audit events. For Dedicated we'll provide integration guidance but HSM may require Private depending on your compliance posture.
[05:42] Elena: Good. Timeline — we're aiming to choose a path in 4 weeks and start POC in mid-April. Any blockers we should be aware of?
[05:51] Ravi: Biggest unknowns are tokenizer parity, any custom kernels in your vLLM fork, and KV cache behavior. If you can share the patched kernel details and sample prompts we can triage early.
[06:06] Samir: We will share a repo pointer for the vLLM fork; some of those patches are internal. Can Redwood sign an NDA for repo access?
[06:14] Maya: Yes, we can — our legal team can run a reciprocal NDA. I'll attach that with the security pack.
[06:23] Toby: About pricing: we care about unit economics at 10M tokens/day. Can you give us a rough delta vs our current spend?
[06:31] Maya: We'll prepare a rough estimate once we have your current token mix and model sizes. But anecdotal ranges: Hosted can be 30–50% cheaper depending on quantization and caching; Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and often lower unit costs at scale. We'll include example numbers in the follow-up.
[06:49] Ravi: For the eval, do you currently run deterministic sampling for your safety/regression tests or do you rely on human evals?
[06:57] Samir: We do both; deterministic for smoke tests, human evals for quality checks. We want to avoid regressions that change heuristic scoring.
[07:06] Maya: We'll preserve your smoke-test harness and run auto-comparison diffs. If you want, we can also run our quality monitors and regression alerts against the same prompts.
[07:18] Elena: Any gotchas moving from a managed vendor that we should be aware of?
[07:24] Ravi: Common gotchas: tokenization drift, slight sampling / RNG differences, and pre/post-processing differences (e.g., text normalization). Also if you use proprietary safety filters from the old vendor, those need mapping. We document those and include bridging configs in the POC.
[07:40] [short silence]
[07:45] Samir: About the vLLM/TGI naming — will Redwood run TGI directly or reimplement parts? We want to keep consistency with our ops.
[07:54] Ravi: We support running TGI-based runtimes and vLLM. We also offer our optimized runtime which behaves similarly but sometimes has different kernel selections; that's why the parity eval is important. We'll give you both: a TGI-compatible path and our optimized path for comparison.
[08:12] Toby: If we opt for Private, how long is provisioning and what's the rollout?
[08:18] Maya: Private deployments vary — VPC options with a private control plane can be as fast as 2–4 weeks for initial deployment in a region if networking and KMS are straightforward; on-prem air-gapped is longer (6–12 weeks) depending on approvals.
[08:33] Elena: That timeline fits. For the POC, we'd prefer Hosted first to validate parity then test Dedicated.
[08:40] Maya: That's very common — Hosted for quick validation, Dedicated for scale and predictable latency, Private for the strictest compliance needs.
[08:50] [20-min mark summary omitted for brevity, call continues with deeper technical checks]
[28:05] Ravi: Quick note on metrics we'll capture: p50/p95/p99, tail latency histograms, token throughput, and tokens per second per GPU. We'll also snapshot KV cache hit rate and memory usage to understand scaling paths.
[28:18] Samir: Great. Also we need to know how Redwood handles function/tool calling and streamed outputs — we rely on streaming heavily.
[28:26] Maya: We support streaming responses and function calling. For streaming we provide chunked responses and backpressure control. We'll include an example stream handshake in the follow-up.
[28:38] Toby: Any friction integrating with our infra-as-code? We use Terraform heavily.
[28:45] Ravi: We provide Terraform modules for Dedicated and Private IAC. For Hosted we have API-based provisioning and a console.
[28:53] Elena: Security question — what about audit retention? Our auditors want 13 months.
[28:59] Maya: We can configure audit retention up to multi-year in Private and Dedicated; Hosted has configurable tiers (30/90/365 days) and we offer add-ons for longer retention.
[29:12] Samir: Ok, let's recap next steps now.
[29:16] Maya: Recap: 1) I'll send the security pack + NDA; 2) Ravi will run an initial micro-benchmark plan once you share the prompt set and the vLLM fork details; 3) Toby to export 7-day latency and token counts; 4) We'll return a rough Dedicated cost estimate and schedule the SE-led test for mid-April.
[29:38] Elena: That works. Any blockers on Redwood signing the NDA quickly?
[29:42] Maya: No, we'll initiate it today.
[29:46] [short laughter]
[29:50] Samir: One small ask — when you do the parity tests, please include the exact seed values and environment snapshots so we can reproduce.
[29:58] Ravi: Absolutely. We'll produce an artifact with seeds, model hashes, and container image tags.
[30:07] Toby: Last question — can we run a cost simulation of 10M tokens/day with quantization turned on?
[30:13] Maya: Yes we'll include that in the pricing follow-up with a few scenarios.
[30:18] [final 15 minutes: logistics and scheduling]
[43:10] Maya: I'll propose two slots for the SE-led test: 2027-04-12 morning UTC or 2027-04-13 afternoon UTC. Which works?
[43:20] Elena: 4/12 morning works for us.
[43:24] Toby: Confirmed.
[43:27] Maya: Great. We'll send invites and the security pack. Anything else?
[43:33] Elena: No, thanks all. Excited to see the parity numbers.
[43:38] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the packet.

Meeting end.

Short action recap (auto):
- Send SOC2/HIPAA pack and NDA
- Run parity micro-benchmark on Hosted vs Dedicated
- Share 7-day latency + token counts
- Provide pricing scenarios for 10M tokens/day and Dedicated reserved capacity

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard technical names (T G I -> TGI, v l m -> vLLM) and some filler words left in.
